The only route authorization the rider gave before departure was a reply at 14:02 to the driver's 14:01 proposal 'ok if I go round by Cavenagh?', which reads as a general consent to take whatever way is faster, not a specific itinerary; it does not authorize driving to Beach Road (F10, F11).

The rider's own request was a quick stop at a 7-Eleven on the way (F11), and the driver did not stop at any 7-Eleven on the route: the sole stationary period is 4 min 10 s at 14:20–14:24 at a point 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off, i.e. away from the corridor (F2) — the driver admits in his own statement that he drove to his '7-Eleven I know on Beach Road' (F14), which the rider never asked for.

Why the stop does not exempt the deviation: the rider named no place in advance and the driver never told the rider before or during the drive which shop he was heading to (F11, F12, F14), so the consent to 'stop at a 711' is consent to a stop only, not to this route change (RD-3(b)); the stop's own duration is not chargeable on a non-taxi service, and here the driver has billed $1.08 of metered waiting (F7) which for the 7.7-minute estimate of a 26.5-minute trip (F3) reflects the detour, not any published Ryde fee.

No traffic exemption is available for the second segment: the only DataMall incident was an accident at 13:52 on Orchard Road towards Bras Basah after Cavenagh Road (0 m from the optimal route, F18), which is on the road the driver had already been authorized to leave, and it sits on the first part of the departure corridor; the segment that ran to Beach Road (F5) is 1553 m off that corridor and is not covered by any incident or severe-congestion band (F16, F17).

claims.assertion: The rider herself, at 14:02, replied to the driver's proposal to go round by Cavenagh with "Okay, sure, go ahead", so the rider agreed before the first off-route segment began at 14:10 (F4, F11, F10).

The driver's stated reason for rerouting is corroborated by a system record: LTA reports an accident on Orchard Road (towards Bras Basah) after Cavenagh Road with two lanes closed, logged 13:52, 0 m from the optimal route, and Orchard Road was in speed band 1 (0-9 km/h) for 14:00-14:10, i.e. before and during the first off-route segment (F18, F15, F4).

The 14:10-14:15 off-route segment (F4) began only 8 minutes after the rider's 14:02 agreement to the Cavenagh route and tracks an accident-blocked Orchard Road corridor, so on the record it is the agreed and justified detour and no refund attaches to it (F4, F11, F18, F15).

Waiting time of 4.2 min billed at $1.08 (F7, F9) is metered waiting at the rider-requested stop on this RydeTAXI trip and is chargeable under the meter, so no waiting component should be refunded (F7, F6, F9).

No rider message agrees to an out-of-the-way drive to Beach Road: the only advance agreement is the 14:02 "Okay, sure, go ahead" plus the 7-Eleven request (F11), and Beach Road appears only in the driver's post-trip statement (F14), which is not rider consent; if the judge reads the record as placing the 14:17-14:29 segment off the rider-requested route, that segment alone (2.87 km, F5) is the maximum exposure.

weaknesses: The rider's 14:02 message named only "a 711 on the way", not Beach Road, and the only fact naming Beach Road is the driver's own post-trip statement F14, which is a statement the system records can outweigh; the tie between the 14:17-14:29 segment (F5) and a road the rider agreed to is therefore weak, and the rider will use F5 and F14 to argue the second segment is unexempted.

The scale is large: actual 9.6 km vs optimal 3.9 km, +5.7 km / +144% (F1), and the trip took 26.5 min against a 7.7 min estimate (F3), which supports the rider's complaint that the route was far longer than necessary.

points.response: The 14:02 'Okay, sure, go ahead' answers a question about a road to avoid, not a route to drive: the driver's 14:01 message names Cavenagh only as the way 'round' a jam on Orchard (F10), so the rider's words leave the route to the driver and amount to a general route authorization, not a named-road agreement (RD-5).

'Ok' at 14:03 accepts a quick stop, not a destination or a road: the driver never named the shop or its location to the rider (F11, F12), and the only stationary point on the track is 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off, i.e. a stop the driver chose off the corridor (F2).

Conceded as to the first part of the corridor: the 13:52 accident at 0 m from the optimal route plus Orchard Road at band 1 from 14:00–14:10 (F18, F15) is exactly the RD-4(a) showing for leaving Orchard Road at the start.

The exemption reaches only the replaced corridor: the incident record covers Orchard Road towards Bras Basah after Cavenagh Road (0 m from the optimal route, F18) and the band-1 record ends at 14:10 (F15), while the loop still runs into a second off-route stretch at 14:17 that is 1553 m off the optimal route (F5) and reaches nothing the rider asked for.

The segment does not end at the requested shop: the rider named no place, and the driver's own statement puts the stop at 'the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road' (F14), never mentioned to the rider in the chat (F11, F12), so under RD-3(b) the extra kilometers of F5 are not exempted by the 'stop at a 711' request (RD-5).

The $1.08 waiting line is 4.2 min of metered waiting consumed by the detour, and the trip ran 26.5 min against a 7.7 min estimate (F3, F7); the driver offers no published Ryde item for an in-trip stop, so nothing about it survives the RD-2 computation on the unexempted segment.

The refund base is the excess distance the meter charged, and RD-2 computes it from the unexempted segment's extra km: $7.99 ÷ 5.67 km = $1.4100/km (F6, F9), so the money item is 2.87 km × $1.4100/km ≈ $4.05 for segment F5, and the rider's own claim of $6.37 (4.52 km) is withdrawn to this figure.

The driver concedes no rider message agrees to Beach Road, and the system record places the F5 segment 1553 m off the optimal route (F5) — so F5 stands as an unexempted deviation; F4 is the only segment the rider's general authorization can reach (F10, F11).

Withdrawn: RD-6 requires an account already carrying an upheld route dispute in 90 days, and the driver's one upheld dispute is a no-show, not a route case (F21), so I no longer ask for flag_account on this record.

The raw deviation figures are correct but not unjustified: the 14:10-14:15 segment (F4) follows the rider's own 14:02 "Okay, sure, go ahead" to the driver's Cavenagh proposal (F11, F10), and the trip ran long because of a documented two-lane closure on Orchard Road with speed band 1 (0-9 km/h) at 14:00-14:10 (F18, F15).

RD-2 refunds only unexempted segment kilometres: segment 1 is exempt under RD-4/RD-5 (F4, F11, F18, F15) and segment 2 carried the rider-requested 7-Eleven stop (F5, F2, F11), so no kilometre component is refundable (F6, F9).

Read as an exchange, the 14:01 ask named Cavenagh and the 14:02 reply "Okay, sure, go ahead" is an agreement to that named road, so this is a named-road authorization, not a general "whichever way is faster" consent (F10, F11).

The rider named no brand or branch; her message says "stop at a 711 on the way" (F11), and the 4 min 10 s stop 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off (F2) is the record tying the 14:17-14:29 segment (F5) to that request, while Beach Road appears only in the driver's post-trip statement (F14).

This is a RydeTAXI trip, so the 4.2 min of metered waiting billed at $1.08 (F7) is chargeable waiting under the meter and the non-taxi in-trip waiting argument does not apply; the stop request in F11 also predates the 14:17 segment start (F5).

I claim no traffic exemption for segment 2; it is exempted under RD-3/RD-5 as the rider-requested stop (F5, F2, F11), while the accident at 0 m from the optimal route (F18) and Orchard Road band 1 during 14:00-14:10 (F15) justify segment 1.

Segment 2 is not an unannounced driver errand: the rider asked for the 711 stop at 14:02 (F11), the driver accepted at 14:03 (F12), and the stationary 4 min 10 s period (F2) sits inside that segment, so the only unmessaged element is which particular shop was chosen (F14).

The driver's profile shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 days and it was a no-show, not a route dispute (F21), so RD-6's precondition of a prior upheld route dispute is not met and no flag_account follows; the rider's clean profile (F20) cannot create one.

My honest fallback stands: if the judge reads the record as placing the 14:17-14:29 segment off any route the rider asked for, the maximum exposure is that segment's 2.87 km at $1.4100/km (F5, F6), about $4.05, not the $6.37 claimed, and my primary case remains that the segment is exempted by the rider's own stop request (F11, F2).

The other detour was not explained by any incident, and your request to stop at a 7-Eleven did not cover the shop the driver picked, which was well off your route. So we are refunding the extra distance from that detour: $4.05, issued as a Ryde voucher to your account. The waiting time at the stop stays on the meter and is not refunded. No further action is needed from you.

We reviewed the disputed trip. Two detours were recorded. The first is excused by a reported accident on the route, so no action on it.
